body:
Deal: Penrite HPR 5 Full Synthetic 5W-40 Engine Oil 5L - HPR05005 $49 + $12 Delivery ($0 C&C/ in-Store) @ Repco

[CheapCookie] I have been considering this for my subaru xv 2017.
It says its compatible in my subaru's book/manual, but I feel it's over kill for my car that will only be doing highway traveling, and might do more harm than good.
engine only has 60k on it.
[smudger] Been using this for about the last 10 years on my 15 year old Renault Fluence. 170,000 kms always worth using a decent oil in your car IMHO decent filter as well
[banana365] Why would it do more harm than good if it's the correct spec?
[CheapCookie] Its thicker oil and I live in Vic(cold climate), it's their max recommendation.
5w-30 is broadly recommended.
The recommended preferred spec is 0w-20.
The 0w-20 is to do with emissions and lower fuel consumption vs engine protection and longevity.
[smudger] https://penriteoil.com.au/
Put your rego in on their website and it will confirm compatibility
[CheapCookie] @smudger: Thankyou.
I did use the rego search and yes my subaru does come up as compatible with their 5w-40.
I've found people mentioning online that subaru have said in other manuals around the world that the 5w-40 was recommend for "sports driving" or heavy towing.
For some reason (I am guessing because of emissions targets) Subaru have put contradicting oil viscosity recommendations in their owners manuals(around the world).
In my manual it says recommended preferred 0w-20 then under that it just has listed 5w-30 and 5w-40 without any explanation.
I only just brought the car a month ago, so it's a little nerve racking.
I just want better engine protection.
[freddofrog42] VIC is hardly a cold climate compared to the ROW. What does your manual state?
E.g. we have a Lexus and that recommends a 5w-30 by default but will also accept a 20W-50 etc. Our old Mazda has 5w-20 on filler cap but the manual recommends 5W-30 and various iterations like 10W-40 and 15W-50 in the manual. 5W-20 does not get a mention in said manual.. CAFE rules for the US market dictate such thins oils.
It's really not that critical for normal cars as long as you change oil every 10/15K and/or yearly. 5W-30 is the defacto standard today but 5W-40 will be just fine as well and might be be a better choice for performance cars and idling ones like taxis etc. There's a reason why the Ford Barra engine used 15W-40 for the taxi LPG and Turbo versions - longevity!
[CheapCookie] @freddofrog42: The manual says recommended preferred 0w-20 then under that it just has listed 5w-30 and 5w-40 without any explanation.
I've found information online where people have said 5w-40 is for sports driving or heavy towing.
The subarus are fussy any other car I would give it ago, but the subarus….they scare me….
As a new subaru owner I am worried 5w-40 will be too thick for daily driving, and will actually strain the pump and cause more wear.
Amazing engine the barra, was considering an engine swap into my old and past Ford Au1 for a while.
[freddofrog42] @CheapCookie: At this point my first thought is well done for reading the manual - so many don't! That's meant as a compliment BTW!
I doubt you would have any issue with 5W-40 to be honest but perhaps hit up some of the more dedicated Subaru Forums to get their take? VIC can get cold-ish but also very HOT so I'd be in favour of the thicker oil.
BTW - Subaru's aren't always that fussy. My late Mon had a bugeye WRX manual until the day she died aged 80… A few "parking by brail" incidents but nothing major. Owned 15 years at least and had done 120k when it was let go after she died.
[Pat317] For most Subarus, 0W-30 or 5W-30 is the way to go.
If it’s high mileage, starting to burn a bit of oil, or gets driven hard in hot conditions, then a 40-grade like 5W-40 is worth considering.
[TrulyUnicorn] The protective benefit of 40-weight oils only really applies when there's sustained hard use, high oil temps, or a worn out engine (and large bearing clearances but that doesn't apply here).
4 cylinder engines with modest power can feel noticeably more sluggish and unresponsive on thick oils, not because you're losing much power but rather they won't rev as freely and there's effectively an added throttle delay. Particularly on a newer engines that run happily on thin oils.
Just run a decent 30-weight if you're not towing and such. 20-weights do in fact offer equal protection despite the online commentary on this stuff, the concern is just that if they shear out of grade you get elevated wear. But for peace of mind just get a 0w30 or 5w30 and call it a day 🤷‍♂️
